summary: Kazuyoshi Kino (1922–2013) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo (1942–1948). He served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (1989), vice-president of Shogen Junior College (1993), and founded Shinnyokai.
Kazuyoshi Soma (born 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Meiji Yamada. In 1987, he was attested as a lecturer at Ryukoku University.
Keenan W. Cox is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Cox earned an MA at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, attested in 2014.

Kees W. Bolle (1927–2012) was a religious studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Leiden, Madras, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. Bolle taught at Brown (~1960–1964) and UCLA (~1969–1994), where he became Professor Emeritus.

Kei Kataoka (born 1969), working in Indology and philosophy, earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo under Hiroshi Marui. After research posts at Oxford, JSPS, and Penn, he joined Kyushu University, becoming associate professor (~2007–2021) and professor (~2021).
Kei Okusa is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate in literature at Otani University, where he is attested as a faculty member in 2026.

Keiichi Miyamoto (born 1948) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned his degrees, including a DLitt, at the University of Tokyo, studying under Minoru Hara. He held posts as lecturer, associate professor, and professor (1995) at Kokugakuin University.

Keiji Iwata (1922–2013) worked in religious studies and related fields. He studied at Kyoto University (1944–1947) and held positions at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1972–1980) and Otani University.

Keiji Nishitani (1900–1990) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied under Kitaro Nishida and Hajime Tanabe at Kyoto University and under Martin Heidegger at Freiburg. He served as associate professor (1935) and professor (1943–1964) at Kyoto University.

Keiki Nakayama specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University (attested 2019–2020), held a JSPS DC2 fellowship (2020), and was attested as a visiting scholar at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Keiki Yabuki (1879–1939) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Taisho University and the University of Tokyo (~1909–1913), he served as professor at Taisho University (1909) and associate professor at the University of Tokyo (~1924–1930).

Keikyo Nakamikado is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. Nakamikado was affiliated with Bukkyo University as a research collaborator (attested 2003) and with the Chion'in Jodo Sect Research Institute as a researcher (attested 2015).

Keinin Hayashi is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He has served as a full-time researcher at the Eastern Institute (attested 1998) and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026), and was formerly a lecturer at Waseda University.

Keir Strickland is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned a PhD at Durham University (~2007–2011) under Robin Coningham. He held academic posts at the University of the Highlands and Islands (2012–2016) and La Trobe University (2016).

Keishin Okamura (1931–2019) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar educated at Kyoto University (~1949–1959). He served as an associate and visiting professor at Koyasan University and as a professor at Kochi University (~1968–1995).

Keisho Tsukamoto (1929–2010) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctorate at Tohoku University (-1964). He served as dean at Rissho University, professor at Tohoku University (~1977–1993), and president of Hosen Gakuen College (~1994–2000).

Keith Dowman (born 1945) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and with traditional teachers including Dudjom Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Kangyur Rinpoche. He held a post at Sonoma State University in 1973.

Keiya Noguchi (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies and completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (~1980–1985). He has held faculty posts at Shuchiin University, becoming professor around 2003, and served as institute director at Taisho University (attested 2017).

Keizaburō Mizuno (born 1932) is a scholar of archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo. He became Professor Emeritus at Tokyo Fine Arts School and served as director of The Niigata Prefectural Museum of Modern Art and Hanzomon Museum.

Ken McLeod (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an MSc at the University of British Columbia (~1968–1970) and studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Dezhung Rinpoche. He taught at Kagyu Droden Kunchab (~1985–1990) and founded Unfettered Mind.
